text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Guntis Ulmanis issued a statement warning that he would bring a suit against leading newspaper Diena unless it withdraws a story which said the president has breached anti-corruption laws. The report came after a string of articles by Diena, revealing that ministers and MPs appeared on the list of various companies as directors despite a law which says they cannot hold both private and official posts.
- Turkish President Suleyman Demirel arrives on his first official visit to Latvia.
- Interior Minister Dainis Turlais wants more information over allegations by the former head of the security police, who said Turlais restricted the activities of the police.

- The newspaper publishes files from the company register, showing two firms where President Ulmanis still formally holds the post of director and president. An official at the register says the companies still formally exist.
- The paper questions if the state revenue service has fulfilled its function of control over the anti-corruption law.

- The leader of nationalist group Fatherland & Freedom said the party may change its mind and not sack Welfare Minister Vladimir Makarov provided the government parties and the prime minister agree to amend the budget so that a new pension law, with which the party disagrees, may be implemented.
- Crude oil and oil products pumped through Ventspils in May dropped by 100,000 tonnes from the previous month.
